concepts.title: Three-Mechanism Model: How Oral Cultures Encode Knowledge
concepts.excerpt: Before writing, humans faced a challenge: how do you store information that matters—genealogies, laws, rituals, astronomical knowledge, agricultural practice—without being able to write it down?

concepts.title: Convergent Evolution: When Different Cultures Invent the Same Solution
concepts.excerpt: Imagine an island culture that needs to preserve genealogies without writing.

concepts.title: Specialization and Initiation: How Restricted Knowledge Preserves Quality
concepts.excerpt: A master genealogist can recite hundreds of names in correct sequence without error.

concepts.title: Literacy Rupture: The Shift from Oral to Written Knowledge Organization
concepts.excerpt: Before writing, knowledge lived in people. A genealogy lived in a genealogist's memory.

concepts.title: The Method of Loci: Spatial Memory as Epistemic Foundation
concepts.excerpt: The method of loci is not a mystical technique or a memory competition trick.

concepts.title: Sacred Sites: Locations as Epistemological Anchors
concepts.excerpt: A sacred site is not merely a location where knowledge is transmitted.

concepts.title: Monumental Knowledge: Permanent Architecture as Knowledge Archive
concepts.excerpt: A genealogy spoken aloud can be forgotten. A ritual performed once will degrade if not repeated.

concepts.title: Portable Memory Systems: Objects That Encode and Carry Knowledge
concepts.excerpt: A monument stands in one place. Its knowledge reaches people who visit it.

concepts.title: Yoruba Ifá: Divination as Knowledge System and Ancestral Communication
concepts.excerpt: A babalawo (divination priest—literally "father of secrets") casts sacred palm nuts or a beaded chain across a wooden board.

concepts.title: Easter Island Moai and Mbudye: Knowledge Collapse and Recovery
concepts.excerpt: Easter Island (Rapa Nui) was settled around 400 CE by Polynesian navigators.

concepts.title: Ancestors as Vessels: Knowledge Transmitted Through Ancestral Presence
concepts.excerpt: In many oral cultures, knowledge is not presented as individual opinion or expertise.

concepts.title: Lukasa: Luba Portable Memory Device and Genealogical Archive
concepts.excerpt: Imagine tracing your family tree not on paper but by running your fingertips across a landscape of ridges and beads.

concepts.title: Performative Memory: Body, Gesture, Song as Cognitive Amplification
concepts.excerpt: When someone describes a spiral staircase verbally, you construct a mental image.

concepts.title: Embodied Memory: Performance, Rhythm, Ceremony
concepts.excerpt: You can read a poem silently and understand it intellectually. You can memorize the words.

concepts.title: Acoustics and Sound in Memory Spaces
concepts.excerpt: Sound travels and reflects. In a closed space—a cave, a kiva, a passage tomb—sound bounces off walls in predictable patterns.

concepts.title: Portable Memory Devices: External Memory Anchors
concepts.excerpt: A carved stone ball from Orkney, 4000+ years old, with intricate geometric patterns.

concepts.title: Stonehenge: Evolving Memory Theatre — Five Phases
concepts.excerpt: Stonehenge was not built once. It was built five times, across 1,500 years, each phase responding to different knowledge transmission problems.

concepts.title: Newgrange and Irish Passage Cairns: Solstice, Genealogy, Permanence
concepts.excerpt: Newgrange is a passage tomb in Ireland, built around 3200 BCE, 500 years before Stonehenge and 1,000 years before the Egyptian pyramids.

concepts.title: Cynic-Pāśupata Greco-Indic Cross-Cultural Hypothesis — Ingalls
concepts.excerpt: A Greek Cynic in fourth-century-BCE Athens carries a wooden club, lives outdoors, deliberately performs scandalous acts in public to attract censure and break his attachment to social opinion.

concepts.title: Daoyin, Qigong, Haṭha-Yoga, 'Phrul-'Khor: Parallel Cross-Tradition Body-Practice Systems
concepts.excerpt: A Chinese practitioner in the second century CE does daoyin — "guiding and pulling" — a set of physical postures combined with breath-work to circulate the body's vital energy.

concepts.title: India-China Alchemy and Sexual-Yoga Transmission Thesis
concepts.excerpt: A bundle of bamboo strips is buried in a Han-dynasty tomb at Mawangdui in southern China in 168 BCE.

concepts.title: Masked Ritual Dance: Cross-Cultural Tantric Performance Traditions
concepts.excerpt: A Tibetan Buddhist monk performs 'cham — masked sacred dance — at an annual monastery festival.

concepts.title: Anthropological Primitivism: Dismantling a Distorting Category
concepts.excerpt: Anthropology inherited from colonial-era explorers a vocabulary of "primitive," "savage," "uncivilized" peoples—terms that seemed descriptive but were deeply judgment-laden.

concepts.title: Genius as Shamanic Archetype
concepts.excerpt: Here is what shamans and artistic geniuses have in common that no one usually says out loud: both are selected by their dysfunction.

concepts.title: WEIRD Psychology: The Ethnographic Scandal of a Science That Studies One Small Tribe
concepts.excerpt: Joseph Henrich's central claim destabilizes the discipline itself: psychology as practiced in Western universities is not the study of human psychology.

concepts.title: Geographic Determinism in Buddhist Transmission: How Landscape Shapes Dharma
concepts.excerpt: In Buddhist history, the specific geography of transmission—the mountains, climate, urbanization, resources, and transportation networks of a region—fundamentally shaped what kind of Buddhism emerged there, what practices became central, what consciousness-states were valorized, and how the teaching was transmitted forward.

concepts.title: Primitive Violence Statistics & Historical Revisionism: Civilization as Violence-Reduction System
concepts.excerpt: Western civilization carries a guilt-driven fantasy: that indigenous and pre-industrial societies were more peaceful, more moral, more harmonious than we are.

concepts.title: Primitivism: Ascending vs. Egalitarian — Two Genealogies, Opposite Directions
concepts.excerpt: Primitivism as a philosophical and cultural movement contains an internal paradox: it claims to return to something "primitive" or "natural," but "return to nature" can mean opposite things depending on which genealogy you follow.

concepts.title: Sleep Paralysis: Neurobiology of Supernatural Encounters
concepts.excerpt: Sleep paralysis is a state where the conscious mind is awake but the body remains in the muscle paralysis state of REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.
